thread:
alok: Seeing an uptick in pod Pending and kubelet errors in us-east-1c around 09:04 UTC. Lots of dns lookup timeouts from kubelets.
marie: confirmed. Health checks failing with `dnsLookupFailed` for several sidecars. Root cause looks like DNS timeouts not DNS resolution errors.
jasmin: node-local-dns on affected hosts has been OOM/restarting a few times, cache hit-rate collapsed. CPU at 100% on those pods.
tj: quick dig from a troubled node:
```
$ dig +time=2 +tries=2 service.internal.svc.cluster.local
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
oncall-net: grabbing tcpdump and path MTU info. Any infra changes recently?
jasmin: we pushed an RDMA offload tweak into the gpu node image last Thursday to improve NVLink throughput. Might be related.
marie: CoreDNS p95 latency spiked at ~09:02, but CoreDNS pods themselves show normal mem/cpu. Most failures appear between pod -> node-local -> coredns upstream.
alok: could be UDP fragmentation on the node-local -> coredns hop. If the vf NIC MTU != veth/overlay MTU we get fragments or ICMP "fragmentation needed".
oncall-net: tcpdump shows lots of ICMP type3 code4 (fragmentation needed) and a stream of UDP retries. Host MTUs: vf eth0=9000, veth=1450, overlay=1400.
tj: that MTU split is bad with DF set somewhere in the stack. With RDMA offload the NIC might be sending jumbo frames that get fragmented by the overlay. If ICMPs get dropped we'll see silent failures.
jasmin: mitigation applied: scaled node-local-dns to 2 replicas per kubelet pool on the impacted nodes and set upstream to TCP for these replicas only. Immediate drop in failures in canary.
alok: TCP upstream avoids UDP fragmentation path but increases latency and CPU load. Keep it for the two affected AZs while we root cause.
oncall-net: opened INC-3977 and cordoned/restarted a few GPU nodes for deeper capture. Collected iperf and traceroute; ECMP paths look asymmetric for some source/dest pairs.
marie: also correlating with increased kube-scheduler queue latency — pods are Pending because liveness/readiness probes cause restarts then backoff. Product teams seeing transient 5xxs.
jasmin: I'll prepare a rollback PR for the RDMA offload flag (#2801) and a one-hour canary before full rollout. Also adding a preflight MTU check to the node-image CI.
tj: created a short dashboard card and alert: node-local-dns upstream failures >3% for 5m. Linking INC-3977.
oncall-net: after disabling RDMA offload on a canary host, packet captures show no fragments and dig returns instantly. node-local-dns CPU normalized.
alok: good. Action list: 1) oncall-net to map MTU/ECMP/firewall drop rules across AZs, 2) infra to rollback RDMA offload on affected pools via #2801, 3) ops to keep node-local upstream as TCP for us-east-1c and us-east-1d until rollback verified, 4) product/console to add node-local cache hit-rate visible to teams.
jasmin: PR #2801 ready, will canary 1 host then ramp. Adding postmortem checklist to validate link MTUs and overlay settings after driver changes.
oncall-net: hypothesis: RDMA offload + inconsistent MTUs + overlay encapsulation -> UDP fragmentation + lost ICMP -> node-local cache upstream timeouts.
marie: reminder: liveness probes using DNS for healthchecks should have local fallback. We'll update probe docs after postmortem.
sre-bot: Incident INC-3977 created by oncall-net. Severity: SEV3. Pager duty notified.
alok: add follow-ups: (a) preflight MTU validation in node image CI, (b) dashboard for node-local error-rate, (c) runbook update for DNS fragmentation cases.
jasmin: will owner postmortem. Will include timeline, MTU checks, CI gate, and the RDMA rollback steps.
oncall-net: keeping TCP upstream on old pools until rollback completes. Observability shows Pending pod count dropping after the canary.
alok: nice work everyone. Postmortem due in 72h; please include suggested guardrails for future NIC/driver changes. :thumbsup:
